findings.title: The offline soundtrack matcher runs before every other offline intent and takes over unrelated requests, sometimes doing the opposite of what was asked
findings.detail: offlineSoundtrack() runs at the top of offlinePlan (right after 'remember'), before translations, captions, lipsync and generate. Its regexes are loose: ONLY includes 'keep', REMOVE_SPEECH matches any 'remove/drop/... <anything> voice' and 'no vocals', and LOWER_MUSIC matches 'turn down ... background'. Verified by calling offlinePlan with a video or audio file attached (scratch vitest, no repo edits): 'Remove the background noise from my voice' + audio -> split_soundtrack keep [music, effects] (keeps the noise and drops the voice, the opposite of what was asked); 'Translate this video to French and keep the voice' -> remove_dialogue keep dialogue (on the base this reached the translate branch at L1170); 'Dub this video into Spanish but keep the music' -> split_soundtrack keep [music]; 'Extend this video and keep the music' -> split_soundtrack; 'Upscale this video, no voice changes' -> remove_dialogue; 'Add captions to this video, keep the voice' and 'Lip sync this video to the audio, keep the voice' -> remove_dialogue keep dialogue; 'Make a music video for this song with no vocals' / 'Write a song like this, no vocals' / 'Generate a video with this audio, no talking' + audio -> split_soundtrack. The make/create/write guard only applies when no file is attached. The tests in tests/assist-soundtrack-tools.test.ts cover only the positive phrases, so none of these false positives is tested.
findings.fix: Either move the soundtrack check after the existing intents (translate/dub/captions/lipsync/generate), or require the soundtrack words to be the request's main verb (e.g. anchor at the start, '^(?:please )?(remove|take out|...)'), drop 'keep' from ONLY unless the sentence names no other operation, skip a remove/lower match when the sentence also names 'noise|echo|hiss|hum' (Clean up voice's job) or another op verb (translate, dub, caption, lip ?sync, extend, upscale, animate, make, create, generate, write), and apply the make/create guard when a file is attached too. Add negative tests for these phrases.

findings.title: The card's time estimate assumes a CPU until something else has read the device, and always says 'on your GPU'
findings.detail: soundtrackTime uses comfyDeviceSeen(), which only reads the cache that comfyDevice() fills. In a fresh server process (or after the one-minute cache entry, which is still read since 'at' isn't checked), a CUDA host's first Assist/MCP card is priced at CPU speed (DBS_SPEED cpu 0.27x vs cuda 22.4x; hostPick(undefined) = fast), so the time is about 80x too long. The wording is always '… on your GPU', even when the device is a CPU. The run's own reply uses previewAudioTool's live device, so only the card is off.
findings.fix: Fire comfyDevice() without awaiting it when planning (so the next card is right), or leave the time out when the device is unknown; say 'on your computer' or 'on your ComfyUI' when the device is a CPU.

findings.title: comfyDeviceSeen was inserted between comfyDevice's JSDoc and comfyDevice
findings.detail: comfyDevice's doc block (L721-724) now sits right above comfyDeviceSeen's own doc block, so comfyDevice has no JSDoc and the orphaned block reads as part of comfyDeviceSeen.
findings.fix: Move comfyDeviceSeen above the existing comment, or below comfyDevice.
